items.title: @random_walker：My best rough estimate of the fraction of the scientific literature that’s wrong — flat-out wrong, you’d-be-nuts-to-rely
items.abstract_or_text: My best rough estimate of the fraction of the scientific literature that’s wrong — flat-out wrong, you’d-be-nuts-to-rely-on-this wrong — is 80%. The problem is that the normal process of scientific self-correction takes time and happens through follow-up work that fails to reproduce experiments, finds computational errors, challenges assumptions, and so on. This is a big opportunity for AI-for-science tools. Agentic interfaces to the scientific literature should be designed so that when they look up a paper they should explicitly look for later work that challenges it.
